idiom_name: ReaderWriterLockSlim with EnterReadLock/EnterWriteLock (+ EnterUpgradeableReadLock) in try/finally
implementation_notes: ReaderWriterLockSlim is the dedicated .NET primitive: EnterReadLock/ExitReadLock (shared), EnterWriteLock/ExitWriteLock (exclusive), TryEnter* overloads with timeouts, and EnterUpgradeableReadLock, which lets exactly one thread inspect state under a read lock and then take the write lock without deadlocking. Use it instead of the legacy ReaderWriterLock (slower and error-prone) and instead of Monitor.Enter/lock, which are exclusive only. The LockRecursionPolicy constructor argument decides whether recursive acquisition is permitted; NoRecursion is the recommended default and makes accidental re-entry fail fast with LockRecursionException. In async code, blocking on EnterWriteLock occupies a thread-pool thread, so SemaphoreSlim or an async lock is usually the better tool there.
pitfalls: Every Exit* must sit in a finally: an exception in the section otherwise leaves a read lock held and blocks the next writer forever.

ReaderWriterLockSlim does not require readers to release from the acquiring thread, so a missing exit is not detected; the default NoRecursion policy turns double-entry into a LockRecursionException instead.
EnterUpgradeableReadLock is not the read lock: only one upgradeable holder may exist, it may not be entered recursively, and mixing upgradeable with plain read locks needs care.
Do not block on EnterWriteLock from async code: a held thread-pool thread plus an awaitable continuation can deadlock the pool.
